problems.title: Two sums from a decreasing arithmetic progression
problems.question: For the arithmetic progression 51,43,..., find (a) the sum of its first 100 terms and (b) the sum of all positive terms.
problems.idea: The common difference is -8. Use the general term to determine when the terms stop being positive.
steps: Here a1=51 and d=-8.
(b) $a_n=51-8(n-1)=59-8n>0$ requires n<59/8. Thus the positive terms have indices 1 through 7, ending at 3.

problems.title: The area outside an inscribed square
problems.question: A square inscribed in a circle has side $4/\sqrt{\pi-2}$. Find the combined area of the four circular segments outside the square.
problems.idea: Subtract the square area from the circle area.
formulas: A square diagonal is s√2 and equals the circle diameter, so R²=s²/2.
Circle area πR²; square area s².
steps: The combined segment area is $\pi s^2/2-s^2=s^2(\pi-2)/2$.
The given side gives $s^2=16/(\pi-2)$.
Substitute and cancel: $16/(\pi-2)\cdot(\pi-2)/2=8$.

problems.title: An odd number of arithmetic-progression terms
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, $a_{17}=9$. Find $S_{33}$.
problems.idea: For an odd number of terms, the average is the middle term.
steps: The middle of 33 terms has index (33+1)/2=17.
Terms equally far from the middle have average a17, so the overall average is 9.

problems.title: The annulus around a regular hexagon
problems.question: A regular hexagon has shortest diagonal m. Find the area between its circumcircle and incircle.
problems.idea: The side equals the circumradius. The shortest diagonal and inradius follow from 30–60–90 triangles.
formulas: For a regular hexagon of side s: R=s, r=√3s/2, and shortest diagonal m=√3s.
steps: From m=√3s, s²=m²/3.
The squared-radius difference is s²-3s²/4=s²/4=m²/12.
Multiply by π to obtain the annulus area.

problems.title: Check whether the requested minimum exists
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, $a_4=1$. For what d is $a_1a_5+a_1a_3+a_5a_3$ smallest?
problems.idea: Express all three terms using d, then check whether the resulting quadratic has a lower bound.
steps: Combine the first two products as $a_1(a_5+a_3)=(1-3d)\cdot2=2-6d$.
The last product is $(1+d)(1-d)=1-d²$.
The expression is $3-6d-d^2=12-(d+3)^2$.
It tends to negative infinity as |d| grows. Therefore it has no smallest value for unrestricted real d.
It has a maximum instead: 12 at d=-3.
problems.answer: No minimum exists. The maximum is 12 at d=-3.
problems.note: The source asks for a minimum. As printed, that request has no solution; changing it to “maximum” would give d=-3. No restriction on d is stated.

problems.title: A square inside a 60-degree circular segment
problems.question: A square is inscribed in a minor circular segment with arc 60°, with one side on the chord and its opposite vertices on the arc. The radius is $2\sqrt3+\sqrt{17}$. Find the square area.
problems.idea: Use a right triangle from the centre to an upper square vertex.
formulas: Centre-to-chord distance for a 60° arc is $h=R\cos30^\circ=\sqrt3R/2$.
steps: Let the square side be s. The upper corner is s/2 sideways from the perpendicular bisector and h+s from the centre.
Substitute h into Pythagoras and multiply by 4: $5s^2+4\sqrt3Rs-R^2=0$.
The positive root is $s=R(\sqrt{17}-2\sqrt3)/5$.
Since R=√17+2√3 and $(\sqrt{17}+2\sqrt3)(\sqrt{17}-2\sqrt3)=5$, the side is s=1.
The area is s²=1.
problems.answer: 1 square unit, for the standard inscribed-square placement described above.

problems.title: Four symmetric roots in arithmetic progression
problems.question: For which real a do the four roots of $(x^2-a^2)(x^2-(a+1)^2)=0$ form four consecutive arithmetic-progression terms?
problems.idea: The roots come in opposite pairs. Four distinct symmetric arithmetic terms have outer magnitude three times the inner magnitude.
formulas: Symmetric four-term arithmetic progression: -3t,-t,t,3t with t>0.
steps: Require either |a+1|=3|a| or |a|=3|a+1|.
The first equation gives a+1=3a or a+1=-3a, hence a=1/2 or a=-1/4.
The second gives a=3(a+1) or a=-3(a+1), hence a=-3/2 or a=-3/4.
Each value gives two distinct nonzero magnitudes in ratio 1:3, so all four roots are distinct and correctly spaced.

problems.title: Triangle-to-sector area ratio
problems.question: A sector and an isosceles triangle share the centre as a vertex, and the triangle’s other two vertices lie on the sector arc. The triangle apex angle is 45°, and the sector angle is 60°. Find triangle area divided by sector area.
problems.idea: Both equal triangle sides are radii, so the unknown radius cancels.
steps: The triangle area is $R^2\sqrt2/4$.
Divide by the sector area: $T/S=(R^2\sqrt2/4)/(\pi R^2/6)$.
Cancel R² and simplify the numerical fraction.

problems.title: Read the printed radical bars carefully
problems.question: Simplify $\left(\frac{a+2}{\sqrt2\,a}-\frac a{\sqrt2\,a+2}+\frac2{a-\sqrt2\,a}\right)\frac{\sqrt a-\sqrt2}{a+2}$, reading the short denominator radical bars literally as covering 2 only.
problems.idea: Use r=√2 to combine the bracket as a rational expression in a. The short radical bars in the scan make the distinction from √(2a) important.
formulas: The original real domain on the literal reading is a>0.
steps: The bracket is $(a+2)/(ra)-a/[r(a+r)]+2/[a(1-r)]$.
The first two fractions combine to $[(a+2)(a+r)-a^2]/[ra(a+r)]$.
Rewrite the third term as $-2(1+r)/a$ and put it over the same denominator. The combined numerator is $-r(r+1)(a+2)$.
Thus the bracket is $-(r+1)(a+2)/[a(a+r)]$.
Multiply by $(\sqrt a-r)/(a+2)$ and cancel a+2. The result is $(r+1)(r-\sqrt a)/[a(a+r)]$.
problems.answer: Literal printed reading: $\frac{(1+\sqrt2)(\sqrt2-\sqrt a)}{a(a+\sqrt2)}$, for a>0.
problems.note: The scan draws each denominator radical bar only over 2, leaving a outside. If those bars were intended to cover 2a instead, the alternative expression simplifies to $1/(\sqrt a+\sqrt2)$ with a>0 and a≠2. These are different questions: at a=2 the literal expression is defined and equals 0, while the alternative original expression is undefined. The interpretation must not be silently changed.

problems.title: Common terms of two arithmetic progressions
problems.question: Find the sum of the first 50 common terms of 2,7,12,... and 3,10,17,....
problems.idea: A common term has the required remainder modulo both common differences; common terms then repeat with the least common multiple.
formulas: First progression: n≡2 mod 5. Second: n≡3 mod 7.
steps: The first common term is 17: it is 2+3·5 and 3+2·7.
The common sequence is 17,52,87,... with difference 35.
